metadata.technology_specification: Triple Quadrupole Liquid Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry (LC–MS) system
metadata.technology_reasoning: The Triple Quadrupole LC–MS system is an industry-standard analytical instrument used extensively for quantitative analysis of complex mixtures, combining liquid chromatography for separation and triple quadrupole mass spectrometry for sensitive and selective detection. It dominates due to its high sensitivity, specificity, and robustness in various analytical fields such as pharmaceuticals and environmental testing.

components.reasoning: Core sub-system responsible for sample separation, typically procured as a complete unit including pump, autosampler, and column oven; universally present in all LC-MS systems.
Central mass spectrometry component with three quadrupole mass filters arranged in series, essential for selective ion filtering and fragmentation; supplied as a dedicated module.

components.component: Ion Source Assembly (e.g., ESI or APCI)
components.reasoning: Primary interface generating ions from eluent, typically electrospray ionization (ESI) or atmospheric pressure chemical ionization (APCI); always present as a distinct assembly.
Includes turbomolecular and backing pumps to maintain high vacuum in the mass spectrometer; critical for instrument operation and usually procured separately.
Detects ions after mass filtering, often an electron multiplier or channeltron; a discrete component essential for signal transduction.
Electronics for controlling quadrupole voltages and instrument operation; often housed in dedicated control units.
Computer and software for instrument control, data acquisition, and analysis; standard component managed separately.
Includes components like ion guides and lenses that transmit ions from ion source to mass analyzer; critical but may be integrated differently depending on design.
